source.title: Mechanistic interpretability of large language models with applications to the financial services industry
source.authors: Ashkan Golgoon; Khashayar Filom; Arjun Ravi Kannan

page_placements.theme: A head's signed role depends on task, readout and analysis method

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures GPT-2 Small head 10.7 in a Fair Lending task, but does not test copy suppression or the other specified claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports head 10.7’s contribution to a prompted Fair Lending classification task. It does not measure repeated-token suppression, calibration, self-repair, or whether copy suppression explains a fraction of loss. Its task-specific results are recorded as related findings, not as tests of those versions.
record.test_reason: The paper applies direct logit attribution and activation patching to GPT-2 Small on a Fair Lending Yes/No prompt task. It never mentions copy suppression, does not cite the original, and measures no suppression of context-present predicted tokens, no calibration and no self-repair. Head 10.7 appears only as one of many heads with large task attributions. The record's 'tests' relation contradicts its own T6 tranche; the correct relation is 'discusses' at most, or effectively unrelated.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that DLA identifies heads 11.4, 8.9 and 6.3 as positive and 0.6, 11.0 and 10.7 as negative contributors. Head-output patching finds 10.2, 10.7 and 11.3 (plus 0.4, 1.7 and 2.1) large positive and 9.6 and 10.6 (plus 0.10 and 5.0) large negative. Head 10.2 matters through its value vector, and layer-0 heads 0.5, 0.1 and 0.10 through their query and key vectors. MLP layers matter much more here than in IOI.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses direct logit attribution and activation patching on Fair Lending prompts. It does not apply a copy-suppression measurement or test the claimed QK/OV mechanism.
record.method_sensitivity: For head 10.7, direct logit attribution describes a large negative contribution, whereas individual-head activation patching describes a very large positive score; these are different analyses and measures.

fits_no_version.finding: On a Fair Lending Yes/No task in GPT-2 Small, head 10.7 has a large negative direct logit attribution. In head-output patching on gender clean/corrupted prompts it has a large positive score.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GPT-2 Small head 10.7 is among the most influential heads on a prompted financial compliance classification task, with sign depending on the analysis method.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on AI in Finance
record.problems: The head-specific results are qualitative, with no reported uncertainty estimates. The activation-patching figures average over 4 prompts, and the study does not test copy suppression or its behavior across ordinary text or the training distribution.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results for head 10.7 were stated in text beyond the direct logit attribution and individual-head patching findings recorded above. The paper's other head and layer results do not concern L10H7.

untested.parts: All of it: L10H7 suppression of predicted, context-present tokens on the training distribution.
All of it: QK/OV mechanism and the fraction of loss effect explained.
All of it: self-repair after upstream ablation.
All of it: negative heads in narrow tasks or other models as copy suppression.
All of it: self-repair mechanism shares.

record.verdict_notes: Head 10.7 (= L10H7) is named, but the paper gives it no functional interpretation and draws no link to copy suppression. The negative DLA sign is loosely consistent with a negative head, but the task answer tokens (Yes/No) are not shown to be copied from context, so it cannot bear on V1. The paper has no controls, no uncertainty estimates and only 4 patching prompts.

versions.untested_parts: Whether L10H7 suppresses context-present predicted tokens across the training distribution, or mainly does so on ordinary text.
Whether QK and OV circuits implement copy suppression or explain 76.9% of its effect on loss.
Whether copy suppression improves calibration by reducing overconfidence in copying.
Whether copy suppression contributes to self-repair after upstream copier ablation.
Whether negative heads in narrow tasks or other models and sizes instantiate copy suppression.
The distribution-wide contribution of copy suppression versus other self-repair mechanisms.
